# Fox News is available in Canada

* This article is more than six years old.
* Published on September 15, 2020 at 19:19
* 1 min read
* By
  Alex CADIER,
  AFP Canada

Posts shared thousands of times on Facebook claims that US cable news channel Fox News is not available in Canada due to media legislation in the country. This claim is false, according to Fox News and one of Canada’s largest television distributors.

“NO Fox News in Canada” says one version of the post, shared more than 20,000 times in Canada across several accounts. It also claims: “The Radio Act makes it a crime to lie to the public via airwaves.”

Image

Screenshot of the post taken on September 15, 2020

Variations of the claim have been shared in the United States and Australia, some as early as 2011.

The core claim that the Fox News Channel is not available in Canada is false.

The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) approved the distribution in Canada of the US-based Fox News Channel in 2004 and according to the Fox News website, the channel is currently available through 16 cable or satellite providers, with two also providing the Fox Business channel.

The CRTC’s website confirms this on its list of “programming services and stations authorized for distribution.”

“We can confirm Shaw Cable and Shaw Direct do indeed carry the Fox News channel for customers in Canada,” Chethan Lakshman, vice president for external affairs at Shaw Communications, Canada’s second largest television provider, told AFP in an email.

The CRTC had previously approved a license for a new Fox News Canada channel in 2003. Fox later chose not to launch the station, writing to the CRTC that “Fox News does not intend to implement this service and therefore will not meet the extended deadline to commence operations.”

**‘Radio Act’**

Hank Intven, Adjunct Professor of Law at the University of Victoria, said by email: “There is no ‘Radio Act’ in Canada. We have a ‘Radiocommunication Act’, but it deals mostly with the radio spectrum, not broadcasting content.”

However, Canada’s Broadcasting Distribution Regulations of 1997 do state that broadcasters cannot distribute a programming service that contains any false or misleading news.

“Fox could be subject to complaints, but it clearly meets whatever basic regulatory requirements are in place to be included within the available broadcast distribution services,” Michael Geist, a law professor at the University of Ottawa told AFP via Twitter.

“Claims that they've been kept out due to the Radio Act are very old and were debunked many years ago,” he said.

Is it true that the FOX news channel cannot be labeled a news channel in Canada?
by E Ash · 2024 · Cited by 66 — Higher Fox News viewership increases incarceration length, and the effect is stronger for Black defendants and for drug-related crimes.

Viral posts celebrating the end of Fox News in Canada appeared on social media in June. Claims Canada blocked Fox News from its airwaves are false. Canada's broadcast regulator says Fox News is still available countrywide and similar claims about the channel's removal have been around since at least 2012. However, in 2023 a Canadian LGBTQ rights group filed an application to have Fox News removed from the list of non-Canadian stations allowed to air in Canada. The consultation process about its removal is still ongoing.

### THE CLAIM

"BREAKING: Fox News is blocked in Canada. Now, number 47 is a nobody … well done Canada," reads a June Threads post with more than 100,000 likes.

### RATING: False

The Fox News Channel is an American conservative television network and website.

The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) approved Fox News on Canada's digital airwaves in 2004.

In an email, the CRTC said Fox News is still available in Canada and the channel appears on a CRTC list of television stations allowed to broadcast in the country.

However, there is a pathway for Canada to block the sometimes controversial channel that consistently tops the list of the most viewed cable news network in the United States, earning 66 per cent of the prime time cable news audience in the first quarter of 2025.

In 2023, LGBTQ rights organization Egale Canada submitted an application to the CRTC to remove Fox News from the list of non-Canadian programming services and stations allowed in Canada.

In its open letter to the CRTC, Egale Canada said former Fox News host Tucker Carlson made false and offensive claims about LGBTQ people on his program. The organization argued his comments violated Canadian broadcasting standards for content exposing a group to hate.

The CRTC received more than 7,000 submissions after calls for public consultation about banning Fox News in Canada.

In a September 2023 response to Egale Canada, then-CRTC secretary-general Claude Doucet said Canada's regulations for non-Canadian television services needed a review, essentially delaying a decision about blocking Fox News until the review's completion.

"A public consultation on the regulatory approach for overseeing non-Canadian television services will start in the coming months," Doucet wrote.

In an email to The Canadian Press, the CRTC said it "intends" to launch a consultation.

"As this matter is currently before the CRTC, it would not be appropriate for the CRTC to comment further," a spokesperson wrote.

For its part, Fox News argued Egale Canada's application was "moot," because the subject of its complaint, Tucker Carlson, was fired in April 2023 and blocking Fox News would be a "grossly disproportionate and unprecedented" response and contrary to the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

There is precedent for banning non-Canadian networks in Canada.

The CRTC removed the Russian state-controlled TV channels RT and RT France from its list of approved non-Canadian programming services after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

In its decision, the CRTC said it was "concerned with programming from a foreign country that seeks to undermine the sovereignty of another country, demean Canadians of a particular ethnic background and undermine democratic institutions within Canada."

Fox News operates a website as well as a cable network. The Fox News website is accessible in Canada, with the exception of Facebook and Instagram due to Meta
